root_cause.text: In netfilter's nft_set_pipapo pipapo_drop(), the loop unconditionally accesses rulemap[i + 1].n for pipapo_unmap() even on the final field, causing a one-past-the-end read from the stack-allocated rulemap array due to call-site argument evaluation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `bool last = i == m->field_count - 1;` and changes `rulemap[i + 1].n` to `last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n`, while the CVE/commit message explicitly states that on the last iteration this read goes past `rulemap[NFT_PIPAPO_MAX_FIELDS]` and is a real out-of-bounds stack read because the argument is evaluated before `pipapo_unmap()` returns early.

intent_record.intent_summary: Record whether the current field is the last one during `pipapo_drop()` iteration so later logic can treat the final field specially.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable `last` is introduced inside the `nft_pipapo_for_each_field(f, i, m)` loop in `pipapo_drop()`, initialized as `i == m->field_count - 1` before the inner `for (g = 0; g < f->groups; g++)` loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this computes and stores whether the current field iteration is processing the final field in `m`. In the shown hunk alone it does not change behavior unless `last` is used later in the function, but it prepares per-iteration state needed to handle the last field differently.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pipapo_drop() to avoid out-of-bounds access to rulemap[i + 1] when unmapping the last field.
intent_record.what: The call to pipapo_unmap() in pipapo_drop() was changed so that its fifth argument is now `last ? 0 : rulemap[i + 1].n` instead of always `rulemap[i + 1].n`, and its sixth argument was simplified from `i == m->field_count - 1` to the existing `last` boolean.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents accessing `rulemap[i + 1]` when processing the last field, passing 0 instead for the next-count value on the final iteration while still marking it as the last field. This avoids out-of-bounds use of the rulemap array and ensures correct unmapping behavior for the terminal field.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is visible directly in `pipapo_drop()`. Inside `nft_pipapo_for_each_field(f, i, m)`, the code unconditionally calls `pipapo_unmap(f->mt, f->rules, rulemap[i].to, rulemap[i].n, rulemap[i + 1].n, i == m->field_count - 1);`. This means `rulemap[i + 1].n` is evaluated for every iteration, including when `i == m->field_count - 1` (the last field). In that final iteration, `rulemap[i + 1]` is one past the end of the stack-allocated `rulemap` array passed into `pipapo_drop()`, matching the described root cause. Although `pipapo_unmap()` itself has an `is_last` parameter and returns early when `is_last` is true (`if (is_last) return;`), that does not prevent the out-of-bounds read because function arguments are evaluated before the call. There is no conditional handling in `pipapo_drop()` to avoid accessing `rulemap[i + 1].n` on the last field, so the fix is not present.
